ver-a1-001: Covet means desire strongly. Admiration, purchase and a request can occur without coveting.
ver-a1-002: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to act; ability, certainty and preparation are different issues.
ver-a1-003: Concise means expressed in few words. A statement can be precise or blunt while remaining lengthy; incomplete means missing content.
ver-a1-004: Obsolete means no longer current or in use; damage, rarity and unpopularity alone do not make something obsolete.
ver-a1-005: Impartial means free of favoritism. A person may be informed and involved yet impartial.
ver-a1-006: Resilient describes recovery after stress or difficulty, not rigid resistance to all change.
ver-a1-007: Frugal means avoiding waste. It does not establish poverty, lack of generosity, or lack of ambition.
ver-a1-008: Candid means honest and direct; candor does not require rudeness, confidence, or informality.
ver-a1-009: Vigilant means alert and watchful; fear or suspicion may accompany it but is not its definition.
ver-a1-010: Plausible means apparently reasonable or believable, without proof or certainty.
ver-a1-011: To coax is to persuade gently, rather than command or simply give an explanation.
ver-a1-012: To scrutinize is to inspect closely; it need not involve memorizing or summarizing.
ver-a1-013: Alleviate means make less severe, not necessarily remove, hide, or delay.
ver-a1-014: Replenish means fill or supply again. Replacing a container or distributing its contents is different.
ver-a1-015: Prohibit means disallow. Regulation or discouragement may stop short of a ban.
ver-a1-016: Nimble means quick and skillful in movement; haste, restlessness or low weight alone is insufficient.
ver-a1-017: Sturdy means strongly built. Something can be heavy or rigid without being strong.
ver-a1-018: Tranquil means calm and peaceful, not necessarily remote, sleepy, or still.
ver-a1-019: As an adjective, elaborate means complex or carefully detailed. Cost or decoration alone does not define it.
ver-a1-020: Inert means inactive or lacking motion; the narrower distractor does not capture the general sense.
ver-a1-021: Tentative means not yet final or certain, hence provisional; it need not be unplanned.
ver-a1-022: A reprieve is a postponement of punishment or temporary relief; it need not remove blame or give permanent immunity.
ver-a1-023: Conspicuous means easy to notice; fame, color and unusualness are possible causes rather than definitions.
ver-a1-024: Wary means alert to possible danger and cautious. Weary concerns tiredness; the other descriptions are too specific.
ver-a1-025: Verify means establish truth or accuracy. Endorsement and repetition do not establish it.
ver-a1-026: Authentic means genuine; counterfeit means made to pass as genuine. Age, rarity and price are not opposites.
ver-a1-027: Rigid means stiff or resistant to bending; flexible is the opposite. Brittleness concerns breaking.
ver-a1-028: Durable means able to last or withstand wear; fragile contrasts with that resistance. Replaceability does not imply fragility.
ver-a1-029: Expand means become larger; shrink means become smaller. The other options describe enlargement.
ver-a1-030: Conceal means hide; reveal means make known or visible. Shelter and retain do not oppose hiding.
ver-a1-031: Optimistic expects favorable outcomes; pessimistic expects unfavorable ones. Realism or caution is not inherently pessimistic.
ver-a1-032: Benevolent means wishing good; malicious means intending harm. Indifference lacks the opposite positive intention to harm.
ver-a1-033: Transparent allows a clear view through; opaque blocks it. Translucent transmits light diffusely and is not the strongest opposite.
ver-a1-034: Voluntary means freely chosen; compulsory means required. Unpaid or deliberate actions can be voluntary.
ver-a1-035: Initial concerns the beginning; final concerns the end. Recent concerns how long ago something happened.
ver-a1-036: Ascend means move upward; descend means move downward. Retreat is backward movement rather than necessarily downward.
ver-a1-037: Mitigate means make less severe; worsen means make more severe. Inaction does not itself name that opposite change.
ver-a1-038: Diligent means showing steady care; negligent means failing to take proper care. Fatigue or inexperience does not establish negligence.
ver-a1-039: Include means have as a part; exclude means keep out. Separating or dividing can leave things included in a larger set.
ver-a1-040: Hostile means antagonistic; friendly is the opposite. Neutral and distant lack hostility without expressing friendliness.
ver-a1-041: Approximate means close but not exact; exact supplies the opposite. Rounded and estimated can be approximate.
ver-a1-042: Perilous means dangerous. Familiarity or predictability does not make something safe.
ver-a1-043: Dormant means inactive, often temporarily; active is the opposite. Slow development is still activity, but is a narrower and less direct choice.
ver-a1-044: Accelerate means increase speed in this everyday sense; decelerate means reduce it, without requiring an abrupt stop.
ver-a1-045: Unanimous means fully in agreement; divided contrasts disagreement. Silence or uncertainty does not establish division.
ver-a1-046: Docile means readily guided or taught; defiant actively resists. Independence alone does not imply defiance.
ver-a1-047: Reinforce means make stronger; weaken means make less strong. Replacement or reshaping need not weaken anything.
ver-a1-048: Legible means clear enough to read; unreadable is the opposite in that sense.
ver-a1-049: Seldom means rarely, so frequently is the opposite. Occasionally is closer to an infrequent rate.
ver-a1-050: Wane means decrease in strength or extent; increase reverses that direction. Fluctuation includes both directions.
ver-a1-051: A glossary explains unfamiliar terms; a map legend explains its symbols. Distances and names can appear on maps without being what the legend primarily defines.
ver-a1-057: Murmur and shout contrast low and high intensity of voice; drizzle and downpour contrast light and heavy rain.
ver-a1-060: The first item is a plan for the second: a blueprint plans a building, and an outline plans an essay.
ver-a1-066: Approval and refusal are nouns naming the respective acts; the other options are an adjective or inflected verb forms.
ver-a1-068: A telescope helps observe distant objects; a microscope helps observe minute, or very small, objects. Nearness alone is not the defining contrast.
ver-a1-070: A hinge permits pivoting movement; an axle provides an axis for rotation. Acceleration, balance and sliding are different functions.
ver-a1-075: Conjecture is a proposed explanation without established proof; the others support or establish a claim.
ver-a1-077: Length, width and height are dimensions; symmetry is a relationship between parts of a shape.
ver-a1-078: An implication conveys something indirectly; the others name explicit statements.
ver-a1-080: A forecast concerns what may happen later; the others concern looking back.
ver-a1-081: Premises, evidence and reasons support an argument; a conclusion is the claim drawn from that support.
ver-a1-082: An appendix is supplementary material; the others name divisions within the main text. The question concerns structural role, not physical attachment.
ver-a1-084: Recede means move back or away; the others describe forward or nearer movement.
ver-a1-085: An encore follows a completed performance; the others prepare for or precede a performance.

ver-a1-056: Insulating reduces heat loss; waterproofing prevents water penetration.
ver-a1-058: An orchard is a source of fruit; a quarry is a source of stone.
ver-a1-059: Whispering is a quiet way of speaking; strolling is a leisurely way of walking.
ver-a1-061: Something fragile is easily shattered; something flammable is easily ignited.
ver-a1-062: One sows a seed and presents evidence; preserve object-to-action order.
ver-a1-063: An opaque material blocks light; soundproof material blocks sound.
ver-a1-064: A composer creates a musical score; a choreographer creates a dance.
ver-a1-065: An anecdote is a kind of story; a sonnet is a kind of poem.
ver-a1-067: A compass indicates direction; a balance scale compares masses.
ver-a1-069: A preface appears at the beginning of a book; an epilogue appears at its end.
ver-a1-071: A liter measures volume; the others measure length.
ver-a1-072: A melody is a sequence of notes, not an instrument.
ver-a1-073: A breeze is moving air; rain, sleet and hail fall from clouds.
ver-a1-074: An atlas is a collection of maps; the other words name life accounts.
ver-a1-076: Clamorous means noisy, whereas the others describe quiet.
ver-a1-079: A glacier is a mass of ice; the others are flowing bodies of liquid water.
ver-a1-083: A rebuke expresses disapproval; the others express admiration.
ver-a1-091: Entry requires sealing; the statement does not require all sealed envelopes to enter.
ver-a1-092: Leading a tour requires training, so Iris completed it. Theo lacks the required training and is not permitted to lead. Training alone does not prove anyone has actually led a tour.
ver-a1-097: Animal handling requires training, so the stated lack of training rules out that role.
